summary.headline: Hester Biosciences standalone revenue rose 28% in Q2 and PAT more than doubled (+131%), with EBITDA margin at 35%.
summary.overview: Management reported standalone revenue up 28% in Q2 and 21% in H1 FY27, with PAT up 131% in Q2 and 108% in H1. Gross margin was 78% and EBITDA margin 35% in both Q2 and H1, despite higher depreciation after the BSL-3 lab and fill/finish facility was capitalised. Consolidated PAT growth (44% in Q2, 71% in H1) was flattered by a Q1 exceptional gain on the amended Hester Africa loan with the Gates Foundation, which management asked investors to view separately. Animal Healthcare H1 revenue fell 14%, while Q2 grew 34% on tender execution.

EBITDA margin Q2 and H1 FY27

segments.name: Poultry Healthcare (Hester India)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 27% in Q2 and 37% in H1 FY27, driven by institutional business, deeper market penetration and customer engagement; H9N2 low pathogenic avian influenza vaccine contributed but was not quantified. Analyst cited poultry at about INR 45 crore of the INR 51 crore six-month consolidated profit.

segments.name: Animal Healthcare (Hester India)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 34% in Q2 on tender execution, but H1 revenue down 14% YoY on lower Q1 sales; government immunisation schedules drive lumpy sales.

segments.name: International (Nepal, Africa)
segments.commentary: Broadly stable with tender, institutional and export supplies across Asia and Africa. Nepal PPR procurement under international eradication programmes did not materialise at expected scale; Hester Africa being built toward consistent business and financial sustainability.

guidance_outlook: Management expects momentum from Q1 to continue into H2 FY27, with poultry the stated base that 'cannot go down'.
Ruminant (large animal) vaccines produced at the Africa plant are a stated focus for future growth, alongside poultry.
Exports expected to rise in FY27 from about 10% of sales in FY26 as new export opportunities are pursued; exports depend on registrations and approvals.
Nepal: management evaluating how to adapt the business and will share developments; working toward a commercially viable path.
Hester Africa: intercompany loan of USD 1 million from Hester India (100% subsidiary) to fortify operations; management says this is not a repayment due date.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation approximately 65% (broad, acknowledged as approximate).
BSL-3 laboratory and fill/finish facility capitalised; depreciation rose as a result.
Future capex possible for technology upgrades and compliance, given regulatory requirements approaching human-health standards; no concrete plan or amount given.
Signed a power purchase agreement for a 3 MW group captive solar project.
Intangible assets under development of about INR 10 crore on standalone balance sheet are R&D costs that cannot be capitalised until commercialisation (per CFO).
demand_pricing: Poultry growth attributed to institutional business, deeper penetration into new areas and technical customer engagement, not a single product event; volume vs price split not given.
H9N2 vaccine: initial India response described as encouraging; management declined to share doses, volumes, revenue or active customer count.
Animal Health seasonality differs from poultry; government programme schedules drive timing.
Regulatory documentation and trial requirements in animal health are rising, which can extend development and approval timelines.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export share of sales after H1 FY27 versus about 9% in the FY26 annual report?
qa_highlights.answer: Priya Gandhi said exports were around 10% last financial year and the ratio should have risen this year given several new export opportunities, without giving a figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the USD 1 million intercompany loan to Hester Africa a sign of more African orders in H2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hester Africa is being strengthened with new registrations across Africa, Middle East and Asia for products made only at the Africa plant; CFO said the 15 November date was the agreement signing date, not a repayment due date.

qa_highlights.question: Will new product launches need large capex, given the fixed asset increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is about 65%; future capex may be needed for technology and compliance upgrades but no concrete plan yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 10 crore intangible asset under development and why is it not expensed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is R&D and licensing spend for product development; such costs are not capitalised until commercialisation, implying capitalisation applies to the asset under development.

qa_highlights.question: Can H2 FY27 match H1, especially in Animal Health?
qa_highlights.answer: Priya Gandhi said that is the aim and momentum from Q1 has held into Q2, but the two segments have different seasonality and product mix.

qa_highlights.question: Is any foreign subsidiary still loss-making?
qa_highlights.answer: Priya Gandhi said no individual entity is loss-making, pointing to consolidated profit growth of about 40%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of poultry growth came from H9N2 versus supplements and disinfectants, and what are H9N2 volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split out H9N2 volumes, doses, revenue or customer counts, saying H9N2 contributed but growth is broad-based across the division.

qa_highlights.question: Is net debt about INR 80 crore (INR 102 crore debt less INR 23 crore cash)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said that view is reasonable, though cash includes balances held for various activities.

risks_watch: Animal Healthcare H1 revenue down 14%; sustainability of tender-led Q2 growth into H2 is unproven.
Nepal PPR procurement shortfall; the business model there is being re-evaluated with no timeline.
Hester Africa still needs financial support (USD 1 million intercompany loan) and operating performance is still being strengthened.
Consolidated profit growth flattered by the one-time Q1 Gates Foundation loan amendment gain.
Possible future capex for technology and compliance; utilisation only about 65%.
Limited disclosure: H9N2 volumes, export share and segment profits not quantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the standalone growth and margin trajectory, but guarded and vague when pressed on H9N2 volumes, Nepal, capex plans and Africa financing. Management repeatedly deferred quantification to later updates.
key_quotes: We are particularly pleased to report a strong growth in PAT, which more than doubled, increasing by 131% during the quarter, and 108% in the first half.

As explained in our previous call, H1 consolidated profitability includes an exceptional accounting gain recognized in Q1 following the amendment of Hester Africa's loan agreement with the Gates Foundation.
In Nepal, the anticipated procurement under international PPR eradication programs has not materialized at the scale originally envisaged.

adds.what: 3 MW group captive solar project (power purchase agreement signed; not production capacity)

growth.why: Standalone Q2 revenue rose 28% YoY and H1 21%, with management expecting Q1 momentum to continue into H2 and poultry as a base that 'cannot go down', but no numeric revenue guidance was given and backing is qualitative (institutional wins, H9N2 vaccine unquantified, exports from ~10% of sales with no figures), while utilisation holds at ~65% and no concrete new capacity was disclosed.
